refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: The MATLAB interface provides a link to the Mathworks MATLAB environment, allowing GMAT to run MATLAB functions as if they were native functions in the GMAT script language.

The Qt optimizer callback connection evaluates the active GMAT optimization sequence and returns numerical results. Callback requests retain that sequence through input transfer, evaluation and result transfer. Function resources cannot be registered as callback services; the connection does not expose a general GMAT function-call operation.

The current Qt MATLAB callback helpers support MATLAB commands inside an optimizer evaluation. GMAT sends that work to the waiting MATLAB callback client, using the same MATLAB base workspace. Typed matrices, logical values, character data, scalar structures and cells keep the interface's existing conversion rules. The C Engine itself is not reentered. Nested work requires the current callback helpers; older clients retain their original evaluation protocol.

Linux Qt MAT-file output assembles independent values before writing and closes its native file handle after each operation. Output produced inside a current MATLAB optimizer callback uses the waiting MATLAB client, so a file can receive data before, during and after that callback. Numeric matrices, jagged cells, string cells and arrays of output records retain their shapes. Version 4 cannot store the writer's structured records and reports an error.

A MATLAB function called by GMAT cannot use legacy script controls or callback commands to start GMAT execution. The restriction applies while MATLAB is evaluating that function or its workspace expressions. Read requests remain available. Independent MATLAB mission controls can build and run scripts while GMAT is idle; they do not provide a direct GMAT-function-call interface.

The shared MATLAB reply API returns owned object and parameter strings without the old fixed-size character limits. Legacy character adapters borrow thread-local storage until their next call and reject embedded NUL data. The modern wx interface owns its encoded reply until the next request and includes the correct text terminator in its byte count. Command data is decoded using the declared text format and size.

Nested Qt optimizer initialization and execution preserve the parent driver's base-workspace values, global values and base/global bindings. Driver inputs, outputs, options and private diagnostics are restored after the child finishes. Callback cleanup also unwinds unfinished child workspace scopes after an error. Unrelated MATLAB variables retain their normal shared-workspace behavior.
The interface cannot be controlled directly through the script language, though it can be in the GMAT GUI. Instead, GMAT starts the interface automatically when it calls a MATLAB function.

There are two GMAT components that provide user access to the interface. For details on declaring a MATLAB function, see the reference. For details on calling a function and passing data, see the reference.

refsection.title: GUI
refsection.para: The MATLAB interface provides an icon in the Interfaces folder in the Resources tree that can be used to control the interface. Right-clicking the icon shows Open, Close, and Engine mode.

Engine mode selects the mode for this GMAT session. On Windows, Shared session uses engOpen and can share a MATLAB engine with other GMAT processes; Private session uses engOpenSingleUse and belongs to this GMAT process. Ordinary function calls and workspace output reuse the same default engine. On Linux and macOS, Session for this GMAT process uses engOpen to start a process-local engine; the C Engine does not attach to an existing session on these platforms. Windows private-session mode is unavailable there. Close active engines before changing the mode; Cancel leaves the current mode unchanged. The startup file's MATLAB_MODE setting still sets the initial mode.

The Open menu item causes GMAT to open a connection to the MATLAB Engine, which in turns displays a MATLAB command window in the background. This connection is then used for all communication between GMAT and MATLAB until the connection is closed. Only one default connection is selected by the GUI. Explicitly named private engines remain available to native API callers on Windows.
The Close menu item causes GMAT to close any open connection to the MATLAB Engine. If no connection is open, it has no effect.

refsection.title: Native object transfer
refsection.para: Native whole-object inputs keep the native serializer's selected properties and owned-object paths. Supported property values travel through typed Engine arrays and cells, including full character data; they are not inserted into MATLAB source as quoted text. A fresh structure is completed before replacing the logical input binding, so fields from previous calls cannot remain as stale input. Function-local declarations participate in this explicit data export. Nested serializers restore their previous mode on completion or error.

Native whole-object MATLAB calls read scalar structure results through the Engine data API. Returned property values retain their numeric precision, dimensions and character data independently of the MATLAB display format or command-window buffer size. Values are captured before GMAT properties are assigned. Unknown and read-only fields are ignored with warnings; invalid writable field types or dimensions cause an error.

Spacecraft tank and thruster lists are prepared together. Omitted lists retain their current attachments, and unchanged names preserve the existing owned components. New attachments are cloned from actual resources resolved in the active scope. Tank links, mass properties and internal estimation references are prepared before the packet replaces displaced hardware. Remove active finite burns before replacing or removing a firing thruster. This grouping does not make other returned properties or objects part of the same transaction.

Nested structures can update existing native owned components. Vectors, matrices and indexed integer lists retain their configured native dimensions. String/reference lists use the native typed list setter: kernel lists, DSN media directories and Formation members support complete replacement, while other providers retain their supported native sizes. Known reference properties bind actual objects; unchanged names preserve existing private bindings. Boolean arrays and Generic values use their native whole-value setters. Native property validation still applies, and a setter error can leave preceding property assignments applied. Main-script parsing and GMAT-function formal argument restrictions retain their existing rules.

refsection.title: Interface Setup
refsection.para: The following conditions must be true for GMAT to successfully initiate communication with MATLAB. All conditions must be true for the same instance of MATLAB.

listitem.para: Install a compatible, licensed version of MATLAB on the same machine on which GMAT is running. GMAT is tested with the latest version of MATLAB at the time of release, though versions R2006b and newer have been known to work.
The architecture (32-bit or 64-bit) of GMAT and the installed version of MATLAB must match. For example, the 32-bit version of GMAT is compatible only with the 32-bit version of MATLAB.

On Windows:
Add the following path (where MATLAB is the path to the installed version of MATLAB) to your Path environment variable (either your user variable, or the system variable). If you continue to have trouble, try putting this path at the very beginning of your system path.
MATLAB\bin\win32 (or win64 for use with 64-bit versions of GMAT)
Register MATLAB for use as a COM server by running:
matlab -regserver
This is done automatically by the MATLAB installer. To do it manually, open an elevated command window and run the command above. Make sure to run the command in the folder containing the executable you wish to use (i.e. MATLAB\bin\win32 or MATLAB\bin\win64.)

On macOS:
Open the MacConfigure.txt in the bin directory and edit the MATLAB_APP_PATH field to point to the location of your MATLAB application bundle.
If the Matlab interface does not work with the GmatConsole command line application, you may need to set up your Terminal so that the system can load the Matlab libraries and start up MATLAB. For example, if you are using a .bashrc, you may need to add something like this:
export MATLAB = <path/to/MATLAB/app/location/>
export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$MATLAB/bin/maci64:$DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH
export PATH=$PATH:$MATLAB/bin
64-bit GMAT must be used to interface with MATLAB after version R2010a.

On Linux:
The MATLAB interface on Linux requires that the C shell, csh, be installed. This is a requirement from the MathWorks for startup of the MATLAB engine, used for the interface. If your system does not have csh installed, the package manager for your Linux installation should include csh as an installation option.
The MATLAB interface needs to be able to locate the MATLAB shared libraries libeng.so (and related libraries) and libMatlabEngine.so. For MATLAB R2019a, the former is in the MATLAB bin/glnxa64 folder and the latter in MATLAB's extern/bin/glnxa64 folder. One way to start GMAT and apply the library path settings is to launch the application with a library path. From the Linux terminal, the command (for MATLAB installed in the default /usr/local/MATLAB/R2019a folder)
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/MATLAB/R2019a/extern/bin/glnxa64:/usr/local/MATLAB/R2019a/bin/glnxa64 ./GMAT
accomplishes this task, starting the GMAT GUI with the settings needed to run the MATLAB interface.
If you are using the officially-released 32-bit version of GMAT, make sure you have the 32-bit version of MATLAB installed.
If the path above exists in your system Path variable, try place it at the front.
Make sure the same instance of MATLAB is referenced both in the Path variable and when running matlab -regserver.

refsection.title: MATLAB Engine Connection

warning.para: Caution: GMAT does not close the MATLAB Command Window it creates after a run has completed. This allows manual inspection of the MATLAB workspace, but it can lead to confusing behavior if MATLAB functions or paths are changed and rerun in the same window.
We recommend closing the MATLAB Command Window by right-clicking Matlab in the Resources tree and clicking Close between each run if you are actively editing the script.

refsection.para: When GMAT runs a mission that contains a MATLAB function call, it opens a connection to the MATLAB engine before it makes the function call. It then reuses this connection for the rest of the GMAT session.
The MATLAB Engine can be controlled manually through the Open and Close options available by right-clicking the Matlab item in the Resources tree.
